raw_response:
I’m 60 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I don’t like making big changes unless I see a clear reason. Our place is only 15 mu, not big, and some people in the family work off-farm, so I have to keep the work manageable and not tie up too much cash at one time. Wheat and maize are still my steady crops. Wheat-maize rotation is what I know best, and it spreads the risk across the year. Cotton can still make money, but it needs more hand work, especially picking, so I won’t put too much land into it. This year I’ll keep most land in wheat-maize and leave a smaller piece for cotton. For fertilizer, I usually do a little more than the bare minimum because if the crop goes yellow or weak, losing yield hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also watch costs, especially irrigation and hired labor. Since I have well water, I can protect the crop when it turns dry, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the crop stage is important.
